sources.title: Random treasure
sources.summary: Random treasure uses constrained value-budget pools. Being eligible means an item can be selected in at least one valid roll for that source; it does not mean the item is guaranteed, or that every candidate has equal final odds.
conditions: The generator rejects explicitly excluded items and items that do not fit the remaining value budget. It stops after filling the budget or exhausting the candidate-attempt limit documented below. Coins are exempt from the minimum-value test, but not the total budget.

Ordinary skeleton, chest, ruin and nest treasure excludes the game's food and material/ignition-item classes. These exclusions include food, wood, rocks, flint, feathers, pelts and several potion ingredients. Do not assume that all inventory items can appear on a skeleton.

The Raving Unwanted and Mutated Unwanted corpse pool deliberately lacks those ordinary type exclusions, but has a much smaller fixed budget. Specific enemy meat/gland drops and the dead camp's fixed supplies are separate systems.

Budget rolls favor smaller outcomes: the game mixes several uniform integer ranges rather than choosing the final budget uniformly. Sampling an item number uniformly at the start does not make final item drop rates uniform after all rejection tests.

Coin selections can grow into a stack through repeated 80% continuation checks, subject to the stack limit and remaining budget. Non-coin items generally receive wear when generated; a full-condition merchant price is therefore not a promise of equal resale value for random loot.
Some otherwise eligible items also have story conditions, shown below. Other explicitly non-lootable records remain excluded even when they have a valid item definition.
sources.image_caption: Coins can appear in random treasure, but the generator is not a guaranteed coin payout.

sources.title: Skeletons and corpses
sources.summary: The randomly placed skeletal remains and partially clothed bodies share the ordinary treasure generator. Their contents are generated when the unopened container is first accessed, rather than being a guaranteed list of equipment or food.
conditions: Outdoor and indoor remains use different value budgets. The same item may qualify indoors but be too valuable for an outdoor body, or too cheap for an indoor body's minimum non-coin value.
The three visual variations are appearances of the same container class, not three independently verified loot tables.
Reopening a searched container does not reroll fresh treasure. Existing contents can deteriorate or disappear as time passes, so eligibility is not a promise about a previously opened body.
These randomly placed remains are not the same as a freshly killed creature's fixed meat/gland drops, the Raving or Mutated Unwanted pool, or the scripted dead-camp containers.
sources.image_caption: Silver is one possible find, not a guaranteed reward from every body.

sources.title: Treasure chests
sources.summary: Some treasure placements become chests instead of skeletal remains. A chest's generated tier controls its value-budget range; those budgets allow a different selection from ordinary bodies.
conditions: The nominal tier-selection rates accompany each pool below. These percentages describe the chest tier, not the odds of finding a particular item.
All three tiers use the same placed-chest sprite in this creation path. The code does not establish a different visible appearance for each tier.
Chests use the ordinary treasure type exclusions. A richer budget does not allow food or every crafting material, and the minimum non-coin value rises with the rolled budget.

The container-kind argument is not the treasure-pool argument: these chests still call the ordinary pool. Do not apply the unused reduced-wear pool branch merely because chest creation uses a numeric kind of two.

pool_refs.condition: Common generated chest tier; 88.2% of generated chests.

Rich generated chest tier; 2% of generated chests.

sources.image_caption: A larger treasure budget can admit more valuable items; it is not a fixed gold reward.

sources.title: Raving and Mutated Unwanted loot
sources.summary: Raving Unwanted and Mutated Unwanted each generate a small random treasure selection when their loot corpse is created. They do not use the same restricted item classes as ordinary world skeletons.
conditions: Eligible food and materials are allowed here, unlike ordinary skeleton treasure. The pool's value-budget and minimum-value rules are documented on Random treasure.

Quantity and final odds depend on the random budget-filling process. No particular eligible item is guaranteed. Recovered stuck arrows are additional to the generated pool, not free newly generated ammunition.

sources.summary: Fallen tree and shrub segments produce their species' wood or berries. Trunks, side branches, size and maturity determine which primary item appears.

conditions: For ordinary trees, the number of generated pieces is the segment's scaled sprite height divided into 16-pixel units, rounded up, plus one. Elderwort uses one piece per fallen segment instead.
Willow and Cypress switch their thin-versus-developed primary wood at a growth factor of 0.2. Bark also requires a trunk or a side branch whose growth factor is above 0.33.
Bramble and Rift Vine berry success increases with growth; there is no single fixed berry percentage for all bushes. Elderwort instead switches to berries at its berry-producing foliage stage.
Green Fingers can add one berry to a successful Bramble, Rift Vine or Elderwort berry drop. Only Bramble and Elderwort berry drops use the special extra-insect path described at Harvested insects.

Living fuel pieces can be wet when they fall. Chopping yields the listed twigs, branches and logs; Firewood is the result of its separate crafting recipes, not the automatic primary yield of every chopped tree.
A branch carrying a beehive has additional Honey and Beeswax; see Beehives.

Bramble and Elderwort berry pieces instead make one check whose chance is 20%, plus 5 percentage points per skill rank, plus 20 percentage points per completed three-rank milestone, capped at certainty. Thus the berry path can find a bug even at rank zero, and reaches certainty at rank eight.
Rare choices are evaluated in order. Later choices require the earlier rare checks to fail; the percentages below include those preceding failures.
The Baby Firelouse selection check is 3% in the ground-plant path but 2.5% in the berry path, before the preceding Glowing Bug failure is included. Do not substitute one path's odds for the other.
Rift Vine berries, beehive products and ash do not use this extra-insect path.

sources.title: Night fireflies
sources.summary: At night outdoors, collectible Firefly patches can appear near the player.
sources.image_caption: A successfully spawned patch contains a small group of Fireflies.
conditions: The outdoor dark-time update can attempt a patch when fewer than five Firefly containers are present. It uses a 50% placement-attempt check and a bounded location search.
Placement still needs a free, non-solid, unoccupied tile within the required distance of the player. A failed search creates no patch.
That percentage is a spawn-attempt check in that update path, not an item drop chance on every player action. Once a patch exists, its initial inventory contains the quantity below.

probability.scope: Conditional on the source and stage described in this row.

rows.condition: Initial contents of a successfully spawned collectible Firefly patch.

sources.title: Story rewards and finds
sources.summary: These scripted story interactions provide particular items. They are separate from ordinary corpse drops, merchant stock and the dead camp's two fixed supply inventories.
sources.image_caption: Ancient Strongbox is found through the library's designated search target.
conditions: This page contains story spoilers. A guaranteed row means the specified interaction gives that item, not that any NPC conversation or any ruin search does so.
The Wooden Recorder comes from the separately interactive dead Unwanted at the camp, not the body pile containing the Herbalist's Belt and not the wooden supply container.

Rift sampling is available at or before Clay's early request for three samples and stops after that quest step. The interaction also requires the player to carry fewer than three Rift Weaves; each successful sample produces one.

Library shelves are initialized with empty search targets and one selected strongbox target. A retrying 2.5% placement check chooses the target; this is not a flat 2.5% chance each time the player searches a shelf.
The Summoning Stone story grants listed here are distinct from its conditional membership in random treasure pools.
